items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names are mostly clear (store.requestAfterSale, updateAfterSaleModalView, openDangerModal). Business code uses single-letter names, e.g. `store.orders.find(o => o.id === ...)` and `for (const it of order.items)`. Comments are sparse in a ~3500-line file.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: One new index.html of about 3500 lines, which caps this at accept. The DOMContentLoaded wiring block is long. The UI reaches into the store directly: `store.cart.items = []; store.cart.appliedCoupon = null; store.save();` in the clear-cart handler skips any store method.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Checkout double-submit is guarded (btn.disabled plus try/finally), import failures are reported in the UI, and empty input is checked. But `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).then(...)` has no catch, and `parseInt(input.value,10) || 0` silently treats bad input as 0.

items.name: Clerk workbench usability: amount breakdown, status hints, dangerous-action confirmation
items.name_zh: 店员工作台可用性：金额明细、状态提示与危险操作确认
items.evidence: Reset uses openDangerModal, cancel is described as confirmed, and checkout has a confirm modal. But 清空购物车 (clear cart) runs with no confirmation. 校验并导入 (validate and import) calls store.importData with no overwrite warning. The after-sale submit refunds immediately with no second confirmation step.

items.name: Business logic lives in one place (UI and test API share it; integer-cent money)
items.name_zh: 业务逻辑集中且被界面与测试接口共用（金额按分计算）
items.evidence: The UI handlers call the same store methods as the API (store.checkout, requestAfterSale, importData), and all 25 hidden tests passed. The clear-cart handler mutates state outside the store. Integer-cent arithmetic can't be confirmed from the visible code.
